evidence.claim: Amnesty reports that throughout 2022 serious attacks on freedom of expression and assembly continued, police used disproportionate and unnecessary force to suppress protests, violence against women and girls remained severe, and Rohingya protection remained a major challenge.
evidence.title: Amnesty International Report 2022/23: The state of the world’s human rights Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty reports that throughout 2022 serious attacks on freedom of expression and assembly continued, police used disproportionate and unnecessary force to suppress protests, violence against women and girls remained severe, and Rohingya protection remained a major challenge.
evidence.source_locator: Bangladesh section and subheadings on expression, assembly, torture, women and girls, refugees
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual rights report with explicit 2022 coverage and Bangladesh-specific findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State conduct under Sheikh Hasina’s administration; the report is country-level but clearly government-related.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes that some legal and policy changes were debated or partially advanced, so the picture is not one of uninterrupted escalation only.

evidence.claim: The report says the 7 December 2022 BNP-police clash left one man dead, more than 50 BNP supporters injured, and several hundred party leaders and activists arrested after police raided the party office.
evidence.title: BNP-police clashes leave one dead as Naya Paltan turns battleground
evidence.excerpt: The report says the 7 December 2022 BNP-police clash left one man dead, more than 50 BNP supporters injured, and several hundred party leaders and activists arrested after police raided the party office.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs and subsequent description of the raid
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting with specific casualty and arrest counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State response under Hasina’s government; while local and immediate, the police action is clearly ruler-period relevant.
contrary_evidence: The report is one event snapshot and does not by itself prove a nationwide pattern, though it fits the broader crackdown record.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that Armed Police Battalion officers beat Rohingya refugees at checkpoints, including people trying to obtain medicine, and described the harassment as part of efforts to coerce refugees toward Bhasan Char or return to Myanmar.
evidence.title: Bangladesh Police Beating Rohingya Refugees
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that Armed Police Battalion officers beat Rohingya refugees at checkpoints, including people trying to obtain medicine, and described the harassment as part of efforts to coerce refugees toward Bhasan Char or return to Myanmar.
evidence.source_locator: Opening paragraphs and the quoted refugee accounts
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous reporting with detailed witness testimony and a clear abuse pattern.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Hasina’s government because the abuse was carried out by Bangladeshi security forces operating refugee policy.
contrary_evidence: The report is specific to camp and checkpoint abuse, not the entire national territory.

evidence.claim: The UN Working Group report cited in the article said allegations of enforced disappearance in Bangladesh rose to 88 in the relevant period, while the government provided information on only eight victims and 81 cases remained unresolved.
evidence.title: Allegations of enforced disappearance increase in Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The UN Working Group report cited in the article said allegations of enforced disappearance in Bangladesh rose to 88 in the relevant period, while the government provided information on only eight victims and 81 cases remained unresolved.
evidence.source_locator: Opening bullet points and the paragraph summarizing the UN report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local reporting on a UN mechanism with concrete numeric findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Hasina’s government because it concerns state accountability for disappearances under her administration.
contrary_evidence: These are allegations and reporting statistics, not final judicial findings on every case.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that, after US sanctions on RAB, the Bangladesh government retaliated against victims’ relatives and human-rights defenders, and that the government used the Digital Security Act and the courts to harass critics.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: Stop Reprisals Against Victims, Activists
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that, after US sanctions on RAB, the Bangladesh government retaliated against victims’ relatives and human-rights defenders, and that the government used the Digital Security Act and the courts to harass critics.
evidence.source_locator: Opening paragraphs and the section on the government response to sanctions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct rights-monitor reporting with specific examples and named targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Hasina government’s response to external pressure and domestic criticism.
contrary_evidence: The same episode also shows international pressure could force some restraint, but the retaliation itself remains the key point.

evidence.claim: HRW said Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina awarded medals and promotions to sanctioned RAB and police officials instead of ensuring accountability, sending the message that abuses would be rewarded rather than punished.
evidence.title: Bangladesh Government Keeps Rewarding Rights Abusers
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina awarded medals and promotions to sanctioned RAB and police officials instead of ensuring accountability, sending the message that abuses would be rewarded rather than punished.
evidence.source_locator: Middle paragraphs discussing promotions and awards
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous human-rights criticism with specific personnel actions and dates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Hasina because the award decisions are described as hers and her government’s.
contrary_evidence: The government could argue it was rewarding service, but the report squarely frames the action as rewarding abusers.

evidence.claim: Amnesty’s Bangladesh overview says freedom of expression, association, and assembly were unnecessarily restricted in 2022, with arbitrary arrests and harassment of critics, while women’s rights, Rohingya conditions, and protection for Indigenous Bawm people remained serious concerns.
evidence.title: Human rights in Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty’s Bangladesh overview says freedom of expression, association, and assembly were unnecessarily restricted in 2022, with arbitrary arrests and harassment of critics, while women’s rights, Rohingya conditions, and protection for Indigenous Bawm people remained serious concerns.
evidence.source_locator: 2022 Bangladesh overview sections and background paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Country-page synthesis of 2022 conditions from a major rights organization.
evidence.period_fit: Summarizes 2022 and is updated as a country overview.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Broadly attributable to the Hasina-era governing environment and its security practices.
contrary_evidence: The overview is broad and summary-level, so it should not substitute for incident-level evidence.

evidence.claim: The UK report says Bangladesh’s human-rights situation remained a serious concern in 2022, but also notes fewer reports of attacks on people because of religion or belief and a reduction in reports of extrajudicial killings and abductions.
evidence.title: Human Rights and Democracy: the 2022 Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office report
evidence.excerpt: The UK report says Bangladesh’s human-rights situation remained a serious concern in 2022, but also notes fewer reports of attacks on people because of religion or belief and a reduction in reports of extrajudicial killings and abductions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official annual foreign-policy human-rights report with explicit Bangladesh section and year coverage.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level assessment of the Hasina government’s domestic safety environment.
contrary_evidence: The same report emphasizes ongoing harassment, detention, media restrictions, and violence against women and girls, so the positive lines are only partial offsets.

evidence.claim: The police citizen charter sets out formal complaint and grievance-redress routes, including GRS escalation, district and metropolitan complaint channels, and women/children/elderly service desks.
evidence.title: Bangladesh Police grievance redress system / citizen charter
evidence.excerpt: The police citizen charter sets out formal complaint and grievance-redress routes, including GRS escalation, district and metropolitan complaint channels, and women/children/elderly service desks.
evidence.source_locator: Section titled 'অভিযোগ ব্যবস্থাপনা পদ্ধতি (GRS)' and the listed complaint services
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official police-service portal describing formal complaint handling.
evidence.period_fit: The page reflects an active grievance system and is consistent with the 2022-2023 service environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional context under the Hasina government, not proof of effective remedy.
contrary_evidence: A formal complaint channel does not prove independence, accessibility, or effective follow-through in abuse cases.
